documentation:
## Snow Aero Graph

### Description

This graph shows how to source Aero smoke on top of an MPM snow simulation in order to add snow dust to capture the affects of the air in snow fracture.

### Inputs, Controls & Outputs

The main control for this graph is a snow ball mesh that controls the location, shape, and size of the snowball. The secondary Aero sim is sourced based on the fracture of the MPM snow particles, which is observed using the change in the `point_firmness` property. The `source_by_firmness_change` compound computes this change and can be edited to customize the sourcing.  The snow particles are voxelized into a signed distance volume which is used as a collider in the aero simulation, that distance field is converted into a mesh for rendering.

The output of this graph are the snow mesh, the aero smoke, the collision geometry all ready to be rendered with Arnold with assigned materials. 

### Workflow and Tips

The `file_cache` compounds are not required. However, it is strongly recommended to cache out the MPM particles and Aero simulations. This makes it very easy to iterate the simulations in isolation and on the meshing and render settings without having to worry about losing a simulation result once everything is dialed in. Also, once cached, the rendering could be easily distributed to a render farm if that is available.

_notes.text:
Render settings:

On the Bifrost shape node, it is ideal that one set:
Arnold --> Translator Options --> Motion blur mode: Velocity Only

This ensures the quickest translate time since the renderer will only be able to use the point_velocity property stored on the mesh.

Arnold:

AA - 3
Diffuse - 2
Specular - 2
Transmission - 2
SSS - 2
Volume Indirect - 2

Adaptive Sampling (Enable)
Max Camera AA - 7

Motion Blur (Enable)
